views.title: Experimental discovery
views.summary: Follow the experiments, observations, and anomalies that forced physics to change—and the later tests that decided whether the new theories survived.
views.narrative: Read downward as a historical argument. Experimental results and unresolved problems motivate theories; later measurements test or support them. Isolated concepts are hidden so the graph emphasizes chains of evidence rather than a complete physics catalog.

views.title: From sets to spaces
views.summary: Trace how bare collections acquire relations, distance, topology, measure, and analytic structure.
views.narrative: This view follows one of mathematics’ central construction patterns: begin with a set, add structure or axioms, and study what becomes possible. It highlights canonical constructions and the induced structures that can be forgotten again.

views.title: Algebraic structures
views.summary: Explore how operations and laws organize groups, rings, modules, algebras, representations, and their categorical relationships.
views.narrative: The emphasis here is structural inheritance: which data are added, which axioms are imposed, and which constructions produce new algebraic objects. Construction diamonds remain visible where several compatible inputs are jointly required.

views.title: Foundations and logic
views.summary: Survey the concepts used to formalize mathematical objects, proof, models, and foundational systems.
views.narrative: This view concentrates on the infrastructure beneath ordinary mathematics: sets, logical languages, models, formal systems, and categorical foundations. It is a compact map of the choices that determine what counts as an object and a valid inference.

views.title: The geometry of gravity
views.summary: Connect differential geometry to spacetime, gravitation, Einstein’s equations, and their classical limits and tests.
views.narrative: General relativity did not merely borrow mathematical notation; it identified gravity with spacetime geometry. This view exposes the mathematical formulations, physical specializations, limiting relations, and experimental evidence surrounding that identification.

views.title: The quantum revolution
views.summary: Move from the empirical crises of classical physics through quantum mechanics, quantum fields, and precision tests.
views.narrative: The quantum framework emerged through a sequence of problems rather than a single deduction. This view combines the motivating experiments with the structural relations among quantum mechanics, field theory, atomic physics, and particle physics.

views.title: Anatomy of the Standard Model
views.summary: Inspect the fields, particles, symmetries, interactions, and measurements assembled into the Standard Model.
views.narrative: Treat the Standard Model as a structured system rather than a list of particles. Follow its gauge framework, matter and force components, interaction terms, classifications, effective descriptions, and decisive collider evidence.

views.title: From classical to relativistic physics
views.summary: See how mechanics and electromagnetism are reorganized by spacetime symmetry and recovered as controlled limits.
views.narrative: Relativity preserved much of classical physics while changing its organizing principles. This view emphasizes specialization, approximation, mathematical formulation, and the experiments that exposed the limits of pre-relativistic models.

views.title: Probability, measure, and analysis
views.summary: Connect measurable spaces, integration, probability distributions, function spaces, and stochastic structure.
views.narrative: Modern probability is built on measure theory and analysis. This view shows the shared carriers and constructions that connect measurable sets, integrals, distributions, random variables, and analytic spaces.
